title: Does Deterministic Generate–Validate–Repair Reduce Unsafe LLM-Generated Network Changes? A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (n=200 intent→configuration tasks) to test whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (GVR) workflow that consults a deterministic network validator reduces validator-detected unsafe network-change incidence relative to an LLM-only generation pipeline. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired reduction in unsafe-change incidence (exact McNemar test). We used a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) with a shared-initial generation semantics, a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a preregistered Mininet emulator holdout as a contamination check. Execution completed with one shared initial model call per task (model_calls_used = 200; preregistered cap = 400). Results: every initial LLM candidate passed the deterministic validator in both conditions (baseline 200/200, GVR 200/200). The paired contingency table is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The preregistered hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported on this task bank. We report the frozen design, execution manifest, exact paired counts, representative examples, and a targeted discussion of operational implications and limitations grounded in archived artifacts (preregistration SHA-256: a9e5d64cbe3a888170d614b971313b4f1550707d39db945843bca930d8caf5d6; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: 191771c3cf89505956e3dba5225397b15f35469951e2222328988b0de22b41d5; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256: eb68aa19ab162c33a6359301700ee9930fb342640a66d8cafc44f65698e693e0; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

sections.introduction: Automating intent-driven network configuration using generative models promises operational efficiency but raises safety concerns: an unsafe configuration can cause outages, policy violations, or security regressions. Prior work proposes grounding LLM outputs with deterministic validators and iterative repair loops (generate–validate–repair, GVR) to mitigate these risks. However, quantitative evidence showing that GVR reduces observable unsafe-change incidence in representative NetOps tasks under an auditable, preregistered protocol remains limited. We preregistered study cnsms2026-gvr-effectiveness-02 to answer the confirmatory question: does a deterministic GVR pipeline materially reduce the incidence of validator-detected unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM-only pipeline on a curated 200-task NetOps intent→configuration bank? Our contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired design (n=200); (2) a completed deterministic execution with archived model calls, validator traces, and emulator contamination checks; and (3) the transparent reporting of a null/negative confirmatory outcome with artifact-grounded operational interpretation and threats-to-validity.
sections.related_work: LLMs exhibit factual errors and prompt sensitivity across domains; mitigation strategies include grounding (RAG), verifier-assisted repair, and bounded agentic architectures. Prototype NetOps systems have used LLMs for intent→configuration translation and paired generation with deterministic checkers (Batfish-style) or emulators. Red-team and configuration-brittleness studies document that agentic tool descriptions, tool-chaining, and persona/history can change safety outcomes. These prior works motivate a confirmatory, preregistered paired evaluation that isolates whether adding a deterministic repair loop to a validator materially reduces validator-detected failures for a given model, prompt policy, and task bank.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary hypothesis: The sealed preregistration (study_id cnsms2026-gvr-effectiveness-02; SHA-256: a9e5d64c...) specified a paired confirmatory design (n=200 tasks), the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), an exact McNemar two-sided test (alpha=0.05), and a maximum model-call budget (400). Task bank and tasks: the confirmatory sample comprised a curated synthetic/public intent→configuration bank of 200 machine-checkable tasks across four topology clusters (50 tasks each). Model and generation policy: the execution contract declared a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and a shared-initial generation semantics (one initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded conditions). The preregistration specified deterministic generation semantics (to reduce stochastic variation). Execution and adapters: the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed the pipeline under the frozen contract. Condition definitions: (A) baseline — apply the single initial generated configuration to the deterministic validator and record pass/fail; (B) guarded/GVR — run the same initial candidate through the deterministic validator and, if violations are reported, issue at most one automated repair prompt to the same model and revalidate. Validator and contamination check: the primary scorer was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (Batfish-style intent/constraint checks); a preregistered Mininet-based emulator served as a secondary disagreement detector on a randomized holdout. Analysis plan: confirmatory analysis used the exact McNemar two-sided test as implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1; secondary estimands (repair iterations, GVR-introduced failures) were exploratory.
sections.results: Execution: the frozen run completed successfully (execution manifest: started_at_utc 2026-08-30T11:50:34Z; completed_at_utc 2026-08-30T12:12:07Z; completed_episode_count = 400, complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 200; maximum_model_calls = 400). Validation outcomes: every initial LLM candidate passed the deterministic validator in both conditions — baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200. The observed 2×2 paired contingency table is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference: paired difference estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0; 95% CI (bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. No pairs were excluded; no technical failures or missing pairs occurred. Repair activity: no validator-detected violations were reported for any initial candidate, so no repair prompts were applied and exploratory secondary estimands are vacuous for this execution. Determinism and provider-call evidence: the execution bundle records that a single shared-initial candidate was used per task and that baseline and guarded responses were identical for each task (representative resource: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA-256 8f38c8becd7e..., baseline and guarded response files identical for task-000001). The recorded model_configuration.json (path execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 a40e96e2...) lists the declared model and related fields; it records "temperature": null. The preregistration required deterministic semantics; although model_configuration.json shows temperature=null, the execution manifest and the response artifacts demonstrate that the shared-initial design produced identical initial candidates across conditions for every task (deterministic_reconciliation provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200). Contamination/emulator holdout: the preregistered contamination detector applied a Mininet-based emulator to a randomized holdout (procedure specified in preregistration). The contamination summary artifact (analysis/contamination_summary.csv, SHA-256 389227f0...) contains no disagreement flags (header only), and no Batfish–Mininet disagreements were observed in the bundled artifacts.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the preregistered hypothesis that GVR would yield a ≥50% relative reduction in validator-detected unsafe changes is not supported on this curated task bank and deterministic execution: both pipelines produced validator-passing outputs for all tasks. This null finding is consistent with three non-exclusive, artifact-supported explanations: (1) under the selected prompts, model, fixed-seed/shared-initial policy, and task bank, the model-generated candidates already satisfied the validator constraints; (2) the primary deterministic validator enforces the task-specified intent constraints and therefore reports no violations for these tasks; and (3) the task-bank hardness or diversity may be insufficient to expose failure modes where repair could help. Operational implication: when an LLM reliably generates validator-passing configurations for the target workload and the validator coverage aligns with operational constraints, adding a GVR repair step may not reduce validator-detected failures. However, this conclusion is narrowly scoped: it does not generalize to different models, higher-temperature sampling, adversarial distributions, broader device diversity, or incomplete validators. Relation to prior work: the result aligns with the literature emphasizing prompt/model/validator sensitivity and the conditional nature of grounding/repair benefits. Reproducibility and artifact pointers: key artifacts are archived and checksummed (preregistration SHA-256 a9e5d64cbe3a..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 191771c3..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 eb68aa19..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 a40e96e2...). Reviewer-requested clarifications resolved from artifacts: (a) model_configuration.json records "temperature": null (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 a40e96e2...); (b) identical shared-initial responses across baseline/guarded are visible in the response artifacts (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA-256 8f38c8be... and the corresponding baseline/guarded response files); (c) contamination_summary.csv (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 389227f0...) contains no disagreement flags, so no Mininet disagreements were observed. Unresolved artifact gaps: the explicit randomized holdout selection seed used for the emulator selection is not present as a standalone labeled field in the publicized artifact set; the preregistration prescribes a fixed-seed selection procedure but the precise selection-seed value is not recorded in a separate manifest entry in the supplied bundle. We report that the contamination summary contains no disagreements and that the holdout procedure was the preregistered randomized fixed-seed method; the absence of a labeled holdout-seed artifact is an explicit reproducibility gap in the bundle.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired study comparing LLM-only generation to a deterministic GVR pipeline on 200 NetOps intent→configuration tasks using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. In this archived execution both pipelines produced validator-passing configurations for every task (paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0). The result shows that, for this model, prompt policy, and task bank, an additional automated repair step did not reduce validator-detected failures because the initial-generated candidates already satisfied the validator checks. This null finding is narrowly scoped; further work must evaluate multiple model families, sampling temperatures, harder/adversarial tasks, diverse real-device behaviors, and validator coverage gaps (emulator or staged production checks) before broader operational conclusions about GVR utility can be drawn.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (mandatory). This study executed under the autonomous-run preregistration cnsms2026-gvr-effectiveness-02 after the autonomy lock defined in the archived master-prompt. LLM and orchestration: experiments used a single hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (provider label: openai_responses), invoked through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family. The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba (immutable archived reference required by the track). Topic constraints imposed by the Research Director limited the study to Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps focusing on safety/reliability of generated network changes. Frameworks and tools: code and experiment orchestration used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 framework and deterministic task-generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). The primary deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (Batfish-style intent/constraint checks). A Mininet-based emulator served as the preregistered secondary disagreement detector on a randomized holdout. Preregistration and freeze: the complete experimental plan (estimand, sample size n=200, paired design, stopping rules, maximum model calls = 400, repair-call budget = 1 per task, shared-initial generation semantics) was frozen before model calls; preregistration manifest SHA-256 is a9e5d64cbe3a888170d614b971313b4f1550707d39db945843bca930d8caf5d6. Autonomous execution and artifacts: the run was performed autonomously under the frozen plan; all model calls, prompts, seeds, validator traces, emulator traces, logs, and artifact hashes are archived in the execution manifest. Key reproducibility identifiers included in the archived bundle are: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 191771c3cf89505956e3dba5225397b15f35469951e2222328988b0de22b41d5), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 eb68aa19ab162c33a6359301700ee9930fb342640a66d8cafc44f65698e693e0), and execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Model-call budget and usage: 200 model calls were used (one shared initial generation per task); up to 200 repair calls were allowed but none were applied because the initial candidates passed the validator. Human involvement: the human Research Director selected the topic family and constraints prior to the autonomy lock; no human manual editing, selective rewriting, or technical changes to the manuscript text occurred after the autonomy lock. Deviations and restarts: no post-preregistration design changes or technical restarts occurred. Limitations and scope: limitations about single-model scope, task-bank coverage, validator completeness, and adversarial robustness are stated in the manuscript body.
limitations: Task-bank scope: the confirmatory sample used a curated synthetic/public intent→configuration task bank (n=200). Results therefore reflect this bank and may not generalize to broader production workloads or adversarial distributions.
Single-model and deterministic setting: only gpt-5-mini (hosted) was tested with the preregistered shared-initial generation policy. Outcomes may differ across model families, temperatures, or seeds.

Validator coverage and oracle limitations: the primary deterministic validator enforces a defined set of syntax/intent constraints; validators can fail to capture real device idiosyncrasies, vendor-specific behaviors, or emergent failure modes detectable only by end-to-end deployment.

Adversarial robustness untested: this confirmatory run did not include active adversarial injection or red-team tool-description attacks; prior audits indicate such vectors can bypass naive defenses and remain a separate concern.

External validity: no production device flash deployment or long-horizon rollout testing was performed; Mininet emulator disagreement checks were included as a preregistered contamination detector but observed no disagreements in this run.

Single repair budget: the GVR pipeline allowed at most one automated repair prompt per task; multi-step repair strategies, different repair budgets, or human-in-the-loop approvals were not exercised here.
